name: CNS Summer Undergraduate Nonproliferation Fellowship Info Session
description:
The CNS Summer Undergraduate Nonproliferation Fellowship is a paid summer program in Monterey. Each year it selects a small cohort of undergraduates from across the country for intensive training in nuclear nonproliferation and disarmament. Fellows carry out their own research projects under the guidance of CNS experts and present their findings at the end of the summer. Through the collaboration between SIGS and CNS, one SUA student will receive priority consideration in the program admission. Come to the session to learn how to apply, what the fellowship involves, and ask questions.
 
If you have any questions, please reach out to us at sigs@soka.edu.

name: “Black Reconstruction & Radical Historiography” with Robin D. G. Kelley & Nahum Dimitri Chandler
description: In “The Propaganda of History,” Du Bois takes on the Dunning School, which portrayed Reconstruction, a radical experiment in abolition democracy, as a failure. In doing so, he lays the groundwork for a critical reassessment of what passes for historical truth. Historian Robin D. G. Kelley, the Gary B. Nash Endowed Chair in U.S. History at UCLA and author of Freedom Dreams: The Black Radical Imagination, Race Rebels: Culture, Politics, and the Black Working Class, and Hammer and Hoe: Alabama Communists During the Great Depression, joins Dr. Chandler for a conversation on radical historiography and the lasting force of Du Bois’s closing argument.

name: Splitting Atoms, Uniting Nations: The Future of Disarmament Diplomacy
description:
Speaker: Jean du Preez, Program Director for Education and Training, Center for Nonproliferation Studies (CNS) at Monterey
 
Nuclear security is shaped not only by weapons and military strategy, but also by diplomacy, treaties, and international cooperation. For decades, the world has relied on the fragile logic of Mutual Assured Destruction to prevent nuclear war. But can we move beyond deterrence based on fear? This discussion explores how a new generation of diplomats, scholars, and leaders can reinvigorate disarmament diplomacy and build a more secure future through dialogue and collective action.
 
Student discussants:
Shota Maeda (’27)
Mateus Cremasco Quesada (’27)
Khuê Anh Nguyễn (’29)

These three students will also speak on December 2, 2026, at a side event to the First Review Conference of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW). The side event is titled “From Learning to Action: The Power of Youth Education for Nuclear Disarmament and the TPNW.”*

name: Fitness Classes: Tabata
description:
Class Description: Tabata is a style of cardio conditioning with 20 seconds of maximum effort, followed by 10 seconds of rest for 4 minutes. We will start with a warm-up, do several intervals and end with a cool down. Good for endurance! 

Fitness Classes are open to all students, staff and faculty! There is no need to sign up for the class, just arrive 5 minutes before the start of class and bring some water! You are welcome to bring your own equipment, yoga mat or tennis racket but if you do not have your own equipment, you are welcome to check the equipment out from the Rec Office, Gym 151.

name: Fitness Classes: Yoga
description:
Class Description: Embodied Flow This one-hour yoga experience blends Vinyasa flow and Pilates-inspired movement to cultivate strength, balance, and release. Each class begins with a moment of intention-setting, inviting you to ground your energy and arrive fully in the body. By integrating breath, presence, and intentional movement, students are guided to move with awareness and acceptance. Sessions emphasize core strength, stability, and increased range of motion. Students of all levels are welcome.

Truth is found in the breath.

Fitness Classes are open to all students, staff and faculty! There is no need to sign up for the class, just arrive 5 minutes before the start of class and bring some water! You are welcome to bring your own equipment, yoga mat or tennis racket but if you do not have your own equipment, you are welcome to check the equipment out from the Rec Office, Gym 151.

name: Richard Marx
description:
Richard Marx is a GRAMMY-winning singer, songwriter, and producer whose career has spanned four decades of chart success and creative reinvention. With over 45 million albums sold, one billion streams, and fourteen No. 1 singles to his name (including “Right Here Waiting,” “Hazard” & “Hold On to the Nights”), Marx is the only male artist in history to have his first seven singles reach the Top 5 on the Billboard charts, and one of only two artists—alongside Michael Jackson—to write a No. 1 song in four different decades. Marx’s work extends far beyond his own recordings, having written and produced for artists including Luther Vandross, Keith Urban, NSYNC, Barbra Streisand and Burt Bacharach.

The evening features Vaughan Williams’ Serenade to Music, a fitting tribute to four decades of artistry.

More info: https://www.performingarts.soka.edu/calendar-events/serenade-music-celebrating-40-years-orange-county-school-arts

Presented by Orange County School of the Arts

name: 2027-2028 Health Professions Application Workshop Series: Part 3
description:
Join the last part of this virtual three-part workshop series to learn how to prepare a competitive application for medical, dental, and veterinary programs. Topics include admissions timelines, testing, school selection, application strategy, committee letters, and interview preparation. 

Workshop 3 will focus on submitting your application | Tuesday, May 4th 16:30 PT
